body:
Closes #6364.

Time interpolation of a `FieldTimeSeries` returned the sample `ψ₁` on an exact hit and `ψ̃ = ψ₂ * ñ + ψ₁ * (1 - ñ)` otherwise; with `Float32` data and `Float64` times those differ in type, and the read inferred as `Union{Float32, Float64}`. Both sites (`time_interpolated_getindex` and the `FractionalIndices` method of `interpolate`) now return `oftype(ψ̃, ψ₁)` on an exact hit, so both branches have the interpolated value's type.

Values are unchanged: the exact hit is converted exactly (`Float32` to `Float64`), and the interpolated branch is untouched. Reads of `Float32` data with `Float64` times are therefore `Float64`, as interpolated reads already were. The alternative is to convert the weight `ñ` to the data's type instead, which makes the reads `Float32` and avoids `Float64` arithmetic in kernels, at the cost of rounding the weight; happy to switch if that is preferred.

**Test.** `test/simulation/output_readers.jl`: for a `Float32` grid with `Float64` times, `fts[i, j, k, Time(t)]` and `interpolate(node, Time(t), fts)` are inferred and correct at an exact hit (`t = 0`) and between snapshots (`t = 0.5`). Not run yet.

title: FieldTimeSeries time interpolation: one return type for an exact hit and an interpolated read

body:
Closes #6345 and closes #6347. Draft.

Two fixes for using a `FieldTimeSeries` at a traced time inside a compiled function on `ReactantState`, both needed to refresh a dataset-backed prescribed atmosphere inside a compiled time step (NumericalEarth/NumericalEarth.jl#816):

1. **`update_field_time_series!(fts::PartlyInMemoryFTS, ::Time)` returns early when the window holds every snapshot** (`start == 1` and `length(fts.backend) == length(fts.times)`), a host check that does not read the time. Such a window never moves, since every index is in it (or past `Nt` under `Clamp`/`Linear`), so nothing changes on any architecture; on `ReactantState` the update no longer fails with a `MethodError` on traced indices (#6345).
2. **`Adapt.adapt_structure(to, ::TimeSeriesInterpolation)` adapts the clock time** with the series instead of storing `f.clock.time` as is. On `ReactantState` that time is traced inside a kernel launch and reached the kernel as a host value, so computing a `Field` of the interpolation (also when building it) failed with an `InvalidIRError` (#6347). `Adapt.adapt` of a plain number is the number, so GPUs are unaffected.

Checked with the MWEs in #6345 and #6347, each with the method redefined: the update compiles with the window unchanged at `InMemory(1, 4)`, and the interpolated `Field` builds and its compiled refresh at `t = 5` gives `2.0`, as on the CPU. Downstream, NumericalEarth's `materialize_geopotential!` (a `Field(TimeSeriesInterpolation(…))` geopotential) compiled on `ReactantState` matches the CPU exactly with fix 2.

Tests: `test/reactant/unit.jl`, a fully resident series updated under `@jit` at a traced time, and an interpolated `Field` on `Clock(grid)` refreshed under `@jit` at a traced time. Not yet run in the test suite.

title: Use a FieldTimeSeries at a traced time: skip full-window updates, adapt the interpolation's clock time
